definition: Of, relating to, or occurring at a solstice; used more broadly to describe anything that seems to pause at its peak before turning back, as daylight does at midsummer.
etymology: From Latin solstitialis, itself from solstitium, the compound of sol (sun) and sistere (to make stand still). The Romans felt the sun literally halt in the sky before reversing its course, and they built the word around that arrested moment. Sistere also gives us armistice, another kind of standing-still.
usage: June 14 sits just a week shy of the solstice, and the evenings already have that solstitial thickness to them, the light lingering past all reason as if reluctant to begin its long retreat.
